stem: Fatty acids are broken down in mitochondria to produce which substance?
rationale: Fatty acids are broken down in mitochondria by oxidation to acetyl-CoA in a process that generates large amounts of energy.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is secreted by liver?
rationale: The liver produces ketone bodies when fatty acid oxidation is proceeding at a high rate.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of diabetes mellitus?
rationale: Diabetes mellitus is a condition that increases fatty acid oxidation.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of ketoacidosis?
rationale: Excess production of ketone bodies over long periods causes ketoacidosis.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of hypoglycemia?
rationale: Inhibition of fatty acid oxidation by hypoglycin leads to hypoglycemia.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Fatty acid oxidation requires the presence of which substance?
rationale: Fatty acid oxidation requires the presence of oxygen.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS OCCURS IN MITOCHONDRIA

stem: Which substance is transported by carnitine across the inner mitochondrial membrane?
rationale: For transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane, acyl groups are transferred from CoA to carnitine by carnitine palmitoyltransferase-I.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS OCCURS IN MITOCHONDRIA > Fatty Acids Are Activated Before Being Catabolized

stem: Which substance is transported by acylcarnitine?
rationale: The acylcarnitine formed is carried into the matrix by a translocase enzyme in exchange for a free carnitine.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS OCCURS IN MITOCHONDRIA > Fatty Acids Are Activated Before Being Catabolized

stem: Carnitine is particularly abundant in which structure?
rationale: Carnitine is a compound that is widely distributed in the body and particularly abundant in muscle.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS OCCURS IN MITOCHONDRIA > Long-Chain Fatty Acids Cross the Inner Mitochondrial Membrane as Carnitine Derivatives

stem: Palmitic acid is converted into which substance after mitochondrial processing?
rationale: For example, after seven cycles, the C16 fatty acid, palmitate, is converted to eight acetyl-CoA molecules.

stem: Palmitate is converted into which substance?
rationale: For example, after seven cycles, the C16 fatty acid, palmitate, is converted to eight acetyl-CoA molecules.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > β-OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS INVOLVES SUCCESSIVE CLEAVAGE WITH RELEASE OF ACETYL-COA > The β-Oxidation Cycle Generates FADH₂ & NADH

stem: Palmitate requires which substance for its activation?
rationale: In the activation step, 2 ATP are used per mol of palmitate.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > β-OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS INVOLVES SUCCESSIVE CLEAVAGE WITH RELEASE OF ACETYL-COA > Oxidation of Fatty Acids Produces a Large Quantity of ATP

stem: Acetoacetate is converted into which substance?
rationale: HMG-CoA lyase then causes acetyl-CoA to split off from the HMG-CoA, leaving free acetoacetate. Both enzymes must be present in mitochondria for ketogenesis to take place.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Acetoacetyl-CoA Is the Substrate for Ketogenesis

stem: Which substance is stored in mitochondria?
rationale: The enzymes responsible for ketone body formation (ketogenesis) are associated mainly with the mitochondria. Acetoacetyl-CoA is formed when two acetyl-CoA molecules produced via fatty acid breakdown condense to form acetoacetyl-CoA by a reversal of the thiolase reaction.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Acetoacetyl-CoA Is the Substrate for Ketogenesis

stem: HMG-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Condensation of acetoacetyl-CoA with another molecule of acetyl-CoA by 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA) synthase forms HMG-CoA. HMG-CoA lyase then causes acetyl-CoA to split off from the HMG-CoA, leaving free acetoacetate.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Acetoacetyl-CoA Is the Substrate for Ketogenesis

stem: HMG-CoA lyase acts on which substrate?
rationale: HMG-CoA lyase then causes acetyl-CoA to split off from the HMG-CoA, leaving free acetoacetate. Both enzymes must be present in mitochondria for ketogenesis to take place.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Acetoacetyl-CoA Is the Substrate for Ketogenesis

stem: Ketone bodies are formed in which structure?
rationale: In mammals, ketone bodies are formed solely in the liver and in the rumen epithelium. 3-Hydroxybutyrate is formed from acetoacetate.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Acetoacetyl-CoA Is the Substrate for Ketogenesis

stem: Which substance is synthesised by the liver from acetoacetyl-CoA?
rationale: In the liver, an active enzymatic mechanism produces acetoacetate from acetoacetyl-CoA. Once acetoacetate is formed, it can only be reactivated by linking directly to CoA in the cytosol.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Acetoacetate requires which substance for reactivation?
rationale: Once acetoacetate is formed, it can only be reactivated by linking directly to CoA in the cytosol. The reactivation of acetoacetate is used in a less active pathway as a precursor in cholesterol synthesis.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Which substance is synthesised by extrahepatic tissues?
rationale: In extrahepatic tissues, acetoacetate is activated to acetoacetyl-CoA by succinyl-CoA-acetoacetate-CoA transferase. CoA is transferred from succinyl-CoA to form acetoacetyl-CoA.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Which substance is transported by coenzyme A?
rationale: CoA is transferred from succinyl-CoA to form acetoacetyl-CoA. The addition of a CoA allows two acetyl-CoA molecules to be formed by the splitting of acetoacetyl-CoA by thiolase.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Coenzyme A is converted into which substance?
rationale: The addition of a CoA allows two acetyl-CoA molecules to be formed by the splitting of acetoacetyl-CoA by thiolase. Two acetyl-CoA molecules are oxidized in the citric acid cycle.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Acetyl-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Two acetyl-CoA molecules are oxidized in the citric acid cycle. 3-Hydroxybutyrate is utilized by converting to acetoacetate, which generates an NADH in the process.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS A HIGH RATE OF FATTY ACID OXIDATION IN THE LIVER > Ketone Bodies Serve as a Fuel for Extrahepatic Tissues

stem: Esterified is converted into which substance?
rationale: In the fed state, FFAs enter the liver cell in low concentrations and are nearly all esterified to acylglycerols and transported out of the liver in very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL).
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS IS REGULATED AT THREE CRUCIAL STEPS

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Jamaican vomiting sickness?
rationale: Jamaican vomiting sickness is caused by eating the unripe fruit of the akee tree. The unripe fruit of the akee tree contains the toxin hypoglycin. Hypoglycin inactivates medium- and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS IS REGULATED AT THREE CRUCIAL STEPS > Impaired Oxidation of Fatty Acids Gives Rise to Diseases Often Associated With Hypoglycemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of dicarboxylic aciduria?
rationale: Dicarboxylic aciduria is caused by a lack of mitochondrial medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS IS REGULATED AT THREE CRUCIAL STEPS > Impaired Oxidation of Fatty Acids Gives Rise to Diseases Often Associated With Hypoglycemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of severe neurologic symptoms?
rationale: Zellweger syndrome causes severe neurologic symptoms. Most patients with Zellweger syndrome die in the first year of life.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS IS REGULATED AT THREE CRUCIAL STEPS > Impaired Oxidation of Fatty Acids Gives Rise to Diseases Often Associated With Hypoglycemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of starvation ketosis?
rationale: Starvation ketosis involves mobilization of free fatty acids (FFA). An exaggeration of the general pattern of metabolism in starvation produces pathologic states in diabetes mellitus.
citation: chapter_22_oxidation_of_fatty_acids_ketogenesis — Oxidation of Fatty Acids: Ketogenesis > KETOGENESIS IS REGULATED AT THREE CRUCIAL STEPS > Ketoacidosis Results From Prolonged Ketosis
